desc: Implement comb-rule best-first heap enumeration (sort A,B,C descending; heapq with negated values; push (i+1,j,k) always, (i,j+1,k) iff i==0, (i,j,k+1) iff i==0 and j==0; all pushes bounds-checked).
Fix the k-increment incremental-value bug: use `dc[k]*(a0+b0)` (not `dc[0]`) for the (i,j,k+1) child in the i==0 && j==0 branch.
Re-validate against the three provided samples (expect 31, 30000, 689589940713840351) — all PASSED.

Verified each cell has a unique predecessor and full reachability; monotonicity (f nonincreasing in each index) guarantees best-first yields correct order statistics; incremental value updates confirmed correct in all branches; index packing fits N<2^18.
Edge cases reasoned: N=1 (only root), K=1, ties handled (equal values sort arbitrarily but K-th largest value is well-defined).
Complexity O(K log K) with ~3 pushes/pop, within N=2e5, K=5e5 limits.
